round1.argument: Decider is CDER in a withdrawal proceeding. No indexed page shows the FDA accepting a new trial as a postmarketing commitment in lieu of withdrawal. The strategist's key page (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.59, printed p. 54) is a risk-factor list of actions the FDA 'may require' in addition to or short of withdrawal; it is Amgen's own hedge, not evidence of an offer-for-approval path, and it says Amgen 'cannot predict whether, or the extent to which, the FDA will consider the information we submitted sufficient'. Worse, the same page and AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.21 (printed p. 16) show the proposal rests on two grounds: lack of substantial evidence of effectiveness AND that the ChemoCentryx application 'contained untrue statements of material facts'. A new randomized trial does nothing for the second ground, and the trial cannot read out inside 24 months, so it cannot cure the first ground on the hearing timeline either. Safety is a third front: p.21 ties the proposal to the March 2026 Drug Safety Communication on fatal DILI cases, and p.59 records label updates on VBDS with fatal outcomes; the registry addresses monitoring, not the benefit side the FDA disputes. AMGN:10k_FY2025.md p.8 (printed p. 2) confirms the FDA's concern is the re-adjudication process for [figure withheld: not gated] of 331 patients plus hepatotoxicity in benefit-risk. The only indexed precedent of the FDA's response to a sponsor's confirmatory data is LUMAKRAS on p.59: a Complete Response Letter plus a new PMR for another confirmatory study, which is an accelerated-approval case and shows the FDA dictates the study, it is not bargained for. Already-announced check (my own search: 'TAVNEOS confirmatory trial', 'TAVNEOS new study', 'TAVNEOS withdrawal hearing' across AMGN filings, transcripts, slides): no new adult trial announced; Amgen's submissions are RWE plus blinded re-adjudication (p.21); the 2026Q2 slides p.11 list an ongoing TAVNEOS Phase 3 in ANCA vasculitis ages 6 to under [figure withheld: not gated], so a trial infrastructure exists but nothing for adults. The move is not announced but it is the obvious textbook sponsor response, which the 10-Q risk factor itself anticipates. Kill signals: hearing denial or summary judgment (Federal Register and 10-Q, measurable, month [figure withheld: not gated] is good; U.S. TAVNEOS below [figure withheld: not gated] a quarter from the 10-Q product table (p.44) is good; enrollment under [figure withheld: not gated] by month 12 is measurable on clinicaltrials.gov but cannot start until the FDA agrees a protocol, so it may trip on FDA delay rather than on the move failing. No promo material, so promo rules not engaged. All strategist quotes verified on their pages.
round1.correction: Narrow to a conditional remedy offer filed into the hearing record: a confirmatory adult trial protocol plus a U.S. hepatic monitoring program, offered as postmarketing requirements the FDA would set, with spend gated. Fund only protocol design, adjudication charter and registry setup (about $10M to $15M [assumption]) until the FDA grants a hearing or signals it would take PMRs in lieu of withdrawal; release the trial budget only then. State in the evidence that the move cannot answer the 'untrue statements of material facts' ground (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.21) and that FDA acceptance is unknowable from indexed pages; the [figure withheld: not gated]-point retention uplift must stay an explicit [assumption] with break-even at about [figure withheld: not gated].

round2.argument: As written ([figure withheld: not gated] committed, a trial offered 'in exchange for keeping TAVNEOS approved') the move is still refuted on the decider: no indexed page shows the FDA trading approval for a new trial, and the proposal's second ground, that the application 'contained untrue statements of material facts' (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.21, printed p. 16), is untouched by any new study. Does the FDA give the gated offer any chance? Some, and I now say so: AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.59 (printed p. 54) lists 'postmarketing commitments or studies' among actions the FDA may require and then speaks of 'any such action or any withdrawal of regulatory approval', which presents PMRs as an alternative outcome to withdrawal, not only an add-on. The same page refutes any quantification: Amgen 'cannot predict whether, or the extent to which, the FDA will consider the information we submitted sufficient'. The first gate is also on p.21: 'If a hearing is not granted, the FDA may enter summary judgment'. So the chance is real but unsourced in size, and it is zero on the untrue-statements ground if that ground alone carries the case. CFO points checked against pages: H1 TAVNEOS U.S. $257M and Q2 $143M are on AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.44 (printed p. 39), so Q1 was $114M and H1 x 2 = $514M is the right base; 'remain on the market during the pendency' is on p.21, so exposure inside 24 months starts only at withdrawal. Margin cite check: the CFO's [figure withheld: not gated] is on AMGN:transcripts/2026Q1_transcript.md p.1 (grade B) and verifies, but it is the Motley Fool summary bullet, not a management quote. Better pages: Peter Griffith, CFO, on AMGN:companies/AMGN/transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.8 (grade B): 'Our non-GAAP cost of sales as a percentage of product sales was 19.6%' (80.4% margin), and the FY2025 reconciliation on AMGN:companies/AMGN/proxy_2026.md p.137: GAAP [figure withheld: not gated] less [figure withheld: not gated] of acquisition-related expenses gives non-GAAP 18.3% (81.7% margin). The [figure withheld: not gated] figure is confirmed to within about a point; it is a company average that includes EVENITY and TEZSPIRE profit share, so it is a proxy, not a product margin. Combining both lenses: with the gated cost (about $12.5M [assumption], midpoint of my $10M to $15M) against the CFO's month-12 exposure of [figure withheld: not gated], break-even is [figure withheld: not gated] = 3.0 points of retention probability, versus [figure withheld: not gated] for the full [figure withheld: not gated]. The gated version is cheap enough that a small, unsourced FDA probability can carry it; the full commitment cannot.
round2.correction: Gated remedy offer in the hearing record: propose a confirmatory adult trial protocol and a U.S. hepatic monitoring program as PMRs the FDA would set; spend about $10M to $15M [assumption] on protocol, adjudication charter and registry setup; release the trial budget only if the FDA grants a hearing or signals PMRs in lieu of withdrawal. Return stated as option value: break-even about 3.0 points on [figure withheld: not gated] of month-12 exposure (H1 run-rate $514M a year at about 80.4% non-GAAP margin, AMGN:companies/AMGN/transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.8); most of the payoff runs after month 24 toward the 1/6/2034 patent. The $345M impairment stays a balance-sheet note, not a second return. Kill: hearing denied or summary judgment entered.

round2.conceded: The CFO is right that the H1 run-rate ($514M a year, p.44) replaces Q2 x 4, that exposure inside 24 months starts only at withdrawal (p.21), that the $345M impairment would double count if used as a return, and that the move is option value with most payoff after month 24. I also concede the FDA gives a gated PMR offer a nonzero chance: p.59 frames PMRs as an alternative to withdrawal. On their framing m01 is the strongest survivor once gated.
round2.held: The FDA's acceptance is not on any page and Amgen itself says it cannot predict it (p.59); the untrue-statements ground (p.21) cannot be answered by a trial; so the candidate as written ([figure withheld: not gated] committed in exchange for approval) stays refuted. The [figure withheld: not gated]-point shift remains a pure assumption.
round2.narrowed: From 'refute the regulatory bargain' to 'support only the gated version': about $12.5M [assumption] at risk, break-even about 3.0 points on the CFO's month-12 exposure, with the trial budget released only on an FDA hearing grant or PMR signal.

steps.reason: Both lenses refuted the move as written. The decider showed no indexed page in which the FDA trades approval for a new trial, and that the proposal's untrue-statements ground cannot be cured by any study (AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p. 21). The CFO showed the run-rate annualized the peak quarter, the full commitment needs a retention gain far above anything sourced, and the impairment avoided double counts the same cash flows. In round two each conceded the other's pages: the CFO accepted the untrue-statements ground and the LUMAKRAS precedent (p. 59); the decider accepted the first-half run-rate, the timing and the non-GAAP margin, and that p. 59 frames postmarketing commitments as an alternative to withdrawal. Both named the same narrowed survivor: a gated hearing-record offer with the trial budget released only on an FDA signal. Still disagreeing: how much probability that path carries. I opened AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p. 21, p. 44 and p. 59, the CFO line on the 2026Q2 call (p. 8) and the proxy reconciliation (p. 137) and confirmed every operand. Ruled narrowed and picked: unrefuted in gated form, not confirmed, because no page prices the FDA response.

The strategist's own cite (2026Q2 transcript p.13) is management saying education is needed, i.e. the plan, not a gap. So the [figure withheld: not gated] is incremental spend on top of an existing campaign and the 3% then [figure withheld: not gated] lift has no indexed baseline to separate it from the current trend (U.S. Repatha +41% in Q2 2026, AMGN:10q_2026Q2.md p.38). Doctor as decider: the evidence shows PCPs already adopting on VESALIUS data, which says the message is landing without this move; it cannot tell whether more exposure changes oral-versus-injection choice. Lipfendra 'direct-to-patient channel' is not on the cited MRK:10q_2026Q2.md p.37 (that page only has the July 2026 approval and label); it is on MRK:10q_2026Q2.md p.32 (Merck 'will be expanding the program in the future to include Lipfendra').
